scopeNote: Zero real vendor/model/native turns. Only B-owned paths. No second coordinator/ledger/lifecycle; original main before-write guard, complete resource proof and barrier untouched. Twelve services, all ledgers, two historical report diffs and untracked b16-real-begin.mjs preserved.
previouslyPassingKept: complete command tuple, 48KB page clamp, known-ref 135540-byte payload over five chunks, strict/exactOptional clean, old control 9/9 - none re-dispatched

largeFirstFrameWasInlineSoRefWasUndiscov.before: a frame bigger than the page budget was emitted as its own oversized inline page, so the caller never saw a reference and discovery failed
largeFirstFrameWasInlineSoRefWasUndiscov.after: a frame larger than the budget is now emitted in REFERENCE form with payload null, the real payloadRef, payloadBytes and a SHA-256 payloadDigest, and the page cursor still advances by that frame's own seq so no frame is skipped or repeated

payloadRouteHadNoProducerBinding.before: possession of the credential plus a ref was enough to read payload bytes
payloadRouteHadNoProducerBinding.after: GET /v1/payload requires an x-pa-producer header carrying the caller's producer; the server validates it against its own registered producer and refuses 409 identity_mismatch otherwise, so a foreign caller cannot read this Runner's payload

lengthReportedBase64CharactersAsBytes.before: the route reported base64 character count as the chunk length
lengthReportedBase64CharactersAsBytes.after: the decoded byte length is reported, and a chunk whose byte length disagrees with the declared total is refused instead of being returned

rfcCorrected.overclaimRemoved: the RFC claimed begin-once, prepared-policy and receiver rules were not bypassed by the socket, and that a pending intent is sent exactly once. Both overstate the actual path: the socket calls the same feed and does not itself add those rules, and exactly-once is not guaranteed. The RFC now says so explicitly and adds unified dispatch to the not-claimed section.
